title: Hubble's 28th birthday picture: The Lagoon Nebula
caption: Part of the Lagoon Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Lagoon Nebula · constellation Sagittarius · about 4000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #18 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This colourful Hubble portrait zooms into a small corner of the Lagoon Nebula, a turbulent star-forming region about 4000 light-years away. The patch is only about four light-years across. The telescope made this image to celebrate its 28th anniversary in space.

To put that in context, the whole nebula is about 55 light-years wide and 20 light-years tall, so Hubble captured just a sliver of it. Star-forming regions like the Lagoon are clouds of gas and dust in which new stars are taking shape, and the energy from those young stars stirs up and lights the surrounding gas, which is why such regions look so restless.

The Lagoon also has a long history on Earth. Italian astronomer Giovanni Battista Hodierna catalogued it in 1654, as part of an effort to record fuzzy objects in the night sky so that nobody would confuse them with comets.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.19 x 4.02 arcminutes) and distance (4000 light years), the frame spans roughly 3.7 × 4.7 light-years. Its light set out about 4,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using filters that isolate the glow of oxygen, hydrogen and nitrogen, along with a broader visible filter. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The narrow filters pick out the light of individual elements, so the colours are a scientific mapping rather than what an eye would see, and the gas is far too faint to view like this directly.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA, STScI
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Since Hodierna's time, the Lagoon Nebula has been photographed and studied by many telescopes and astronomers around the world. Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 gathered the observations for this picture over about a week in February 2018.
alt: A colourful, turbulent region of glowing gas and dust within the Lagoon Nebula.
